newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kia-Turk Ihlas venture to break ground in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Kia-Turk Ihlas venture to break ground in Turkey.

text.p: Turkey's Ihlas Holding said it and South Korea's second largest auto maker Kia Motors would start work on Thursday on the plant to build KIA brand cars and commercial vehicles in Turkey.
Construction of the plant in Duzce, around 200 km east of Istanbul, was planned to be completed in late 1998 at a cost of $175 million at 1996 prices.
The output target for the venture is 100,000 Sephia cars, 10,000 Ceres pick-ups as well as Pregio panelvans and caravans.
A 25 percent initial local share in the production is planned to be raised to 70 percent levels in the following years, Ihlas said.
It added that 1,500 people would be employed at the plant.
Turkish President Suleyman Demirel will attend the ground breaking ceremony on Thursday, Demirel's press office said.
Ihlas Holding which has a wide range of activities from finance and media to food and marketing, currently distributes and markets Kia brand cars in Turkey.
The venture was set up in August 1996 with a 3.9 trillion lira capital. Its 55 percent stake is held by Ihlas, 15 percent by Kia and 30 percent stake by Japanese general trader Nichiman Corp.
